clue.text: Appearance perhaps initially in a religious group

indicators.note: in tells us the next letter goes inside the word for a religious group

parts.note: a sect is a religious group

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of the word perhaps is used

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a person looks as if they belong to some religious sect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes P from 'perhaps'; 'in' puts it inside A + SECT, after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspect is the look or outward appearance of something, as in a house of pleasant aspect.

clue.text: A duck and a single — maybe similarities?

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters could be arranged in some other way

parts.note: a duck is a score of nought in cricket, O

explanation.surface: A cricketer's nought and a scored run might just look alike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' mixes A, O and A SINGLE; a duck is a cricket score of zero, shaped like O.
explanation.definitionFit: Analogies are likenesses or correspondences drawn between things.

clue.text: Bill North at the back door

parts.note: a bill is a poster or notice

explanation.surface: A man called Bill North is standing at the rear entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' reads as a man's name; it is a poster.
explanation.definitionFit: A postern is a small rear gate or private entrance, especially in a castle.

clue.text: Plain tale (for a spell) of a high church feature

parts.note: clear means plain, evident
a story is a tale

explanation.surface: A simple narrative, read to cast a spell, about some feature of a lofty church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a spell' says the two words are spelt together; 'high church' suggests ritual but means high up in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A clearstory, usually spelt clerestory, is the upper row of windows in a church nave.

clue.text: His wife was no finished web weaver

definitions.text: His wife was no finished web weaver

parts.words: His wife was no finished web weaver
parts.note: Homer's hero's faithful wife wove a shroud by day and unpicked it by night to delay her suitors, so her weaving was never finished

explanation.surface: A man's wife never managed to complete the cloth on her loom.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Odyssey Penelope promised to remarry once her weaving was done, then secretly undid it every night.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek king of Ithaca was the husband of Penelope, the weaver who never finished.

clue.text: Set off in old hat, carrying sort of crop

indicators.note: carrying means the word for old hat holds the other word inside it

parts.note: old hat means outmoded, dated
an Eton crop is a short boyish haircut

explanation.surface: Someone wearing an ancient hat is laden with some kind of harvest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crop' suggests farming; the Eton crop is a 1920s short haircut, named after the English public school.
explanation.definitionFit: To detonate is to explode, so a charge that has been set off has detonated.

clue.text: Willingly putting all that together

parts.note: the phrase and so on means all that, everything of the sort, giving its last two words
the phrase and so on means all that, everything of the sort, giving its last two words

explanation.surface: Gladly combining everything mentioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all that' stands for 'and so on'; 'putting together' joins SO and ON into one word.
explanation.definitionFit: As in I'd as soon stay, the word means as gladly or as readily.

clue.text: Shown up like those on a Brighton beach?

definitions.text: like those on a Brighton beach?
definitions.meaning: Brighton has a well-known naturist beach where bathers are uncovered

explanation.definitionFit: Exposed means unmasked, and also bare to the elements like a nudist.

clue.text: Flowers perhaps watered by this

definitions.meaning: a small bunch or sprig of blooms
fine droplets thrown from a hose or can

explanation.definitionFit: A spray is a sprig of blossom and also a jet of fine droplets for watering.

clue.text: Old clothes, singularly, may go up in smoke

definitions.meaning: a widow's mourning garments are her ..., so one garment in the singular
tobacco or cannabis that is smoked

explanation.definitionFit: Widow's weeds are mourning garments, and the word is also slang for tobacco or cannabis.

clue.text: Severely simple direction to follow the wind

indicators.note: to follow puts the compass direction after the name of the wind

parts.note: Auster is the classical name for the south wind
E is east, a compass direction

explanation.surface: Instructions to walk downwind, written in the plainest terms.
explanation.walkthrough: AUSTER, the Roman south wind, is not everyday knowledge; it is a crossword stalwart.
explanation.definitionFit: Austere describes something plain and strict, without ornament or comfort.

clue.text: An example of swearing

parts.note: the idiom 'swear like a ...' names a cavalry soldier as the model of foul language

explanation.surface: A request for a sample of bad language.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavalry soldier is the stock comparison in the idiom for heavy cursing.

clue.text: Ended up as most important

parts.note: over means ended, as in the match is over
up can mean on horseback, as a jockey is up, so riding

explanation.surface: Something finished up being the chief priority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' for RIDING is a racing usage: the jockey 'up' is the one riding the horse.
explanation.definitionFit: An overriding concern is one that takes precedence over all others, the paramount one.

clue.text: Gray has a fling

parts.note: a shy is a throw or fling, as at a coconut shy

explanation.surface: Someone called Gray is having a brief romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fling' looks like an affair; it is a shy, a throw, as at a fairground coconut shy where balls are thrown at coconuts.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ashy is the pale grey colour of ash; Gray is the American spelling.

clue.text: Sport about a posh new dress

parts.note: re means about, concerning
a creation is a fashion designer's new garment

explanation.surface: Games played around an elegant new gown.
explanation.definitionFit: Recreation is leisure activity or play, which is one sense of sport.

clue.text: Re gin and it cocktail that causes internal combustion

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so these letters are mixed up into a new order

explanation.surface: About a gin and it cocktail, a drink that sets one's insides on fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cocktail' mixes the letters of RE GIN IT (the 'and' is only a link); gin and it is gin with Italian vermouth.
explanation.definitionFit: An igniter is a device that sets fuel alight, as the spark that fires an engine's cylinders.

clue.text: Like something that has been gone over before

definitions.text: Like something that has been gone over before

parts.words: Like something that has been gone over before
parts.note: ground that has been walked across again, trampled a second time

explanation.surface: Describing a matter that has already been discussed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone over' suggests discussion; it means walked over, trodden again.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground walked on a second time has been trodden again, so the path is well worn.

clue.text: Cloth, the French style, we hear from a fiddler

parts.note: tweed is a woollen cloth
le is the French word for the, the French way of saying it

explanation.surface: A woollen fabric in the Parisian fashion, and the sound coming from a violinist.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is what a listener hears from a fiddler: the thin sound of a violin being played.
explanation.definitionFit: To tweedle is to play a fiddle or pipe idly, and the word also names that thin sound.

clue.text: Means of getting out men in jet, etc, disaster?

indicators.note: a disaster leaves things in disorder, so these letters are scattered into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: How crew escape when an aircraft full of men meets catastrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disaster' mixes MEN JET ETC; the 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ejectment is the act of casting out, especially the legal action to remove an occupier from property.

clue.text: Water-parsnip about to be eaten by common woman

indicators.note: to be eaten by means the word for about goes inside the word for woman

parts.note: skirt is a vulgar slang term for a woman
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A water plant is about to be consumed by a coarse lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'common woman' is dated, dismissive slang for a woman; 'to be eaten by' says the short word for about sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Skirret is a perennial plant of the carrot family grown for its sweet roots, also known as water-parsnip.

clue.text: Fashionable kid, America's nightmare

parts.note: in means fashionable
a cub is a youngster, as a cub reporter
US is the United States

explanation.surface: A trendy youngster is the bad dream of the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: An incubus is a demon thought to lie on sleepers, so a crushing bad dream.

clue.text: It may be vile — cure, and change

indicators.note: change tells us to alter the order of the letters of cure and

explanation.surface: Something nasty might be remedied, and then altered.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the stock phrase 'durance vile', meaning harsh imprisonment.
explanation.definitionFit: Durance means imprisonment, and the stock phrase is durance vile.

clue.text: Leader, roughly offensive

parts.note: the leader is number one, No 1, written NOI
some means roughly, as in some twenty people

explanation.surface: The chief is somewhat rude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader' is No 1, read as NO plus I; 'roughly' is SOME, as in some ten miles.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisome means foul-smelling or objectionable.

clue.text: Tube's avoided, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells us the word for avoided is to be taken by its sound

parts.note: ducked means avoided, dodged

explanation.surface: Someone skipped the London Underground, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tube' looks like the London Underground; it is the definition, a pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A duct is a pipe or channel carrying air or fluid.

clue.text: Vision of note — in drink

indicators.note: in places the musical note inside the word for drink

parts.note: a dram is a small drink of spirits
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A sight seen after a famous tune in a glass of whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of note' points to a single musical letter, and 'in' puts it inside the small measure of whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: A dream is a vision seen in sleep or an imagined ideal.

clue.text: One I met going to St Ives

definitions.text: One I met going to St Ives

parts.words: One I met going to St Ives
parts.note: the nursery rhyme 'As I was going to St Ives, I met a man with seven wives'

explanation.surface: A traveller recalls a stranger met on the road to a Cornish town.
explanation.walkthrough: St Ives is a Cornish seaside town; the rhyme's man with seven wives has many wives at once.
explanation.definitionFit: The man in the rhyme had seven wives, so he was a man with several spouses at once.

clue.text: A long time? Long? Not quite

indicators.note: not quite means the word for long falls short by its last letter

parts.note: to yearn is to long for

explanation.surface: Asking whether a long time is really so long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' trims the last letter from YEARN.
explanation.definitionFit: Twelve months can feel like an age, so the period serves as a lengthy span.

clue.text: Westminster has good opening for a draught

parts.note: SW1 is the London postcode for Westminster, read as SWI

indicators.note: opening means the first letter of the word good

explanation.surface: Parliament gives a fine start to a cold breeze.
explanation.walkthrough: SW1 is the postal district of Westminster in London, with the numeral read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A swig is a large gulp of drink, a draught in the drinking sense.

clue.text: The Spanish type submitted to being jostled

parts.note: el is the Spanish form of the definite article
bowed means submitted to, yielded

explanation.surface: A Spaniard of some kind gave in to being pushed about.
explanation.definitionFit: Elbowed means pushed or shoved aside with the elbows, roughly jostled.

clue.text: First year puzzle carrying weight

parts.note: the first year of the Christian era is AD 1, written ADI
to pose is to puzzle or baffle

explanation.surface: A first-year student's teaser concerning weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First year' is AD I, the year one in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: Adipose means fatty, so the description fits a body that is overweight.

clue.text: Hatred not shown by male 24

parts.note: a man with many wives can hardly be accused of loathing women

explanation.surface: A man with many wives clearly bears no grudge against the opposite sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 24 is the answer to 24 across, the man met on the way to St Ives.
explanation.definitionFit: Misogyny is hatred of women, which no man with seven wives could be said to feel.

clue.text: Achilles thus resolved to sulk here

definitions.meaning: in the Iliad Achilles sulked in his tent, so he was in a tent
determined, firmly set on a purpose

explanation.surface: The Greek hero made up his mind to go and brood in his quarters.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as IN TENT, it describes Achilles sulking in his tent during the Trojan War.
explanation.definitionFit: Being intent on something is being determined; split in two the word says where Achilles sulked.
